ac:layout-cell.h1: B2B Router Provider Adapter Binding Solution Specification
ac:layout-cell.p: Terminology follows the shared e-invoicing glossary. This document is a proposed provider binding. It does not approve B2B Router as the Phase 2 pilot, select a contracted API version, or prove that Sage has production entitlement.

This specification binds B2B Router to the shared Phase 2 connection, routing, invoice and recovery design. It defines what a Sage-managed B2B Router adapter must prove before pilot and production. It does not copy the shared platform design or make B2B Router concepts the Sage domain model.
Part 2 defines the logical behaviour. Part 3 defines interactions and data. Part 4 defines acceptance evidence and release gates. REF Source references identifies the exact source and its limits.
The labels in this document have these meanings:

The design is reviewable but needs approval or implementation evidence.
A named owner must supply a decision or evidence before the affected gate can pass.
Another feature owns the behaviour or the first adapter release excludes it.
Product outcomes, provider discovery requirements, business rules, acceptance expectations and gates.
Consultation-ready, not delivery-ready. Public documentation does not prove Sage entitlement or Spain production eligibility.

ac:layout-cell.p: The current public documentation is newer than the provider PRD review. It documents API version 2026-06-26, received-invoice webhook events, new import behaviour and revised environment guidance [B2BR-S02–S05]. This specification treats that version as an evidence candidate, not the selected build version. The selected version remains B2BR-Q01.
In scope:

ul.li: bind one B2B Router account scope to one authorised Sage connection scope;
qualify outbound, inbound, lifecycle, document retrieval and reconciliation separately;
execute an approved JSON-create or structured-file import strategy;
receive authenticated webhooks and recover missed observations through bounded reads;
preserve requested and actual provider transport/document-type facts;
keep route change, credential change, provider deregistration and historical release as separate actions;
preserve raw provider states and derive Sage lifecycle views under a versioned mapping.

ac:layout-cell.p: Open for the first delivery cohort: contracted product/version, Spain registration and reachability, account/legal-entity cardinality, payload strategy, supported directions and formats, status provenance, idempotency, retention, service targets and exit sequence.

Out of scope: VeriFactu and other tax-report operations; provider commercial contracting; automatic route failover; per-invoice caller override; Private A → Private B customer switching; provider-side implementation; and direct B2B Router integration in each Sage ERP.

tr.td: Provider connection
Sage configuration that references an approved B2B Router account scope, credential, environment and API version. It is not the active route.
Account scope
The stable B2B Router account, group or other contracted resource that owns the operation. The exact mapping is open.
Contract profile
The approved operation, API version, environment, authentication, payload, transport/document rules and recovery behaviour.
Provider observation
A response, webhook or retrieved record from B2B Router. It is stored with source, time, version and provenance.
Actual exchange values
The transport and document type returned or observed after provider processing. They can differ from requested values and must be checked.
Reconciliation window
A bounded, overlapping invoice-list query used to detect missed observations. Its checkpoint advances only after durable classification.
Customer authority and route activation
Shared Identity, Onboarding and Routing owners. The adapter cannot activate itself.
Connection/profile qualification
Shared Connection owner with the B2B Router adapter owner.
Provider credential protection
Trust/credential owner under SPEC-SEI-001. Adapter contracts use a credential reference only.
Outbound invoice/action
SPEC-SEI-007 owner. The adapter executes only its assigned exchange action.
Inbound source capture
SPEC-SEI-016 owner. The adapter supplies authenticated source bytes and metadata.
Raw event and derived lifecycle
SPEC-SEI-009 owner. The adapter preserves provider facts and does not define customer meaning alone.
Unknown outcome and missed event recovery
Adapter + shared resilience/Operations owners. One operation has one reconciliation owner.
Spain product scope and provider acceptance
Spain Product/Compliance plus provider owner. Public API availability is insufficient.

ac:layout-cell.p: Reuse of a proposed pattern is not proof that a deployed implementation is fit. Every candidate needs an actual build, contract, owner, gap record and test evidence before activation.
Editable Draw.io · PNG preview.

The flow starts when the shared platform supplies an authorised and version-bound action. B2BR-01 checks the provider binding. B2BR-02 freezes the selected provider operation and payload. B2BR-03 executes it once. A known response goes to B2BR-04. A possible external effect with no reliable result goes to B2BR-07 before any repeat. Webhooks accelerate observation through B2BR-05, while B2BR-06 performs independent bounded reconciliation. B2BR-08 preserves historical access after route change. Tax reporting stays outside the binding.

tr.td: B2BR-01 Qualify provider binding
Connection owner checks account scope, environment, API version, credential reference and each requested capability. It saves evidence without changing a route.
Connection/adapter owner records failed or unknown checks and required action.
B2BR-02 Prepare provider action
Exchange/Receiving supplies immutable route/action context. Adapter selects the approved operation, representation and requested transport/document values.
Adapter rejects missing or mismatched profile data before an external call.
B2BR-03 Execute provider operation
Adapter records durable intent, then performs the selected read or mutation with explicit version and correlation.
A pre-transmission failure can retry within policy. A possible external effect enters B2BR-07.
B2BR-04 Record provider response
Adapter saves request ID, provider invoice ID, returned state, actual transport/document type and redacted errors. Owning feature records the independent result.
Unknown or incompatible returned values create a discrepancy; they do not silently complete the action.
B2BR-05 Process provider webhook
Ingress authenticates, timestamps, deduplicates and correlates the raw event before lifecycle interpretation.
Invalid, expired or uncorrelated events enter quarantine. They do not change customer state.
B2BR-06 Reconcile missed observations
Scheduled or incident-triggered worker reads a bounded overlapping window. It captures missing provider facts and advances the checkpoint after durable classification.
Pagination ambiguity or provider outage keeps the previous safe checkpoint and raises an owned backlog.
B2BR-07 Resolve unknown outcome
Reconciler searches the original account/version/context. It links one proven match, repeats only after proven absence and safe-repeat evidence, or leaves an owned unresolved case.
Operations owns manual decision and evidence. It cannot choose a new provider or operation silently.
B2BR-08 Preserve continuity and release
Route changes stop new selection. Earlier invoices retain provider context and permitted retrieval/status access until approved release.
Exit/Records blocks deregistration or credential destruction while dependencies remain.

ac:layout-cell.p: The most material risks are wrong account scope, silent provider fallback, duplicate mutation, webhook gaps, overstatement of provider states, cross-environment key use, coupling to tax reporting and loss of historical access. Part 4 contains the blocking decisions. No implementation commitment should precede B2BR-Q01–Q04.

tr.td: B2BR-I01
A validated connection does not activate a route.
B2BR-I02
Authenticated caller, represented party, B2B Router account scope and credential scope are separate facts.
B2BR-I03
Each capability and direction is qualified independently for one environment and contract version.
B2BR-I04
The adapter uses an explicit approved API version. It does not rely on a mutable group default.
B2BR-I05
The owning feature saves immutable invoice/action context before the adapter can create an external effect.
B2BR-I06
One exchange action has one execution owner and one reconciliation owner.
B2BR-I07
Provider API acceptance, asynchronous processing, provider send, recipient delivery, buyer decision, payment and reporting are separate outcomes.
B2BR-I08
Requested and actual provider transport/document values are preserved. An incompatible substitution blocks progression.
B2BR-I09
A possible external effect is not repeated until reconciliation or proven idempotency makes the action safe.
B2BR-I10
Raw provider facts remain available after mapping. Unknown states remain unmapped until approved.
B2BR-I11
Webhooks are not the only source of completeness. Independent reconciliation is required.
B2BR-I12
Route change does not rewrite old invoice context or automatically revoke historical access.
B2BR-I13
Provider tax-report identifiers remain separate and cannot activate tax reporting.
B2BR-I14
Spain rules remain in the Spain binding and cannot become shared or provider defaults.

ac:layout-cell.p: Proposed internal operation states are PREPARED, IN_PROGRESS, OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, OBSERVED_SUCCEEDED, OBSERVED_FAILED, HELD and CLOSED. These are Sage recovery states, not B2B Router values. The actual implementation owner must map them to existing stores under B2BR-Q08 rather than create a duplicate operation store.

B2BR-01 — Qualify provider binding. The request names tenant, represented legal entity, environment, integration role, direction and capability. The Connection owner verifies the authenticated principal and current authority. The adapter checks only approved, non-mutating provider operations unless a separately owned setup mutation exists. It records the intended and observed account scope, explicit API version, credential version, supported operation, provider codes, observation time, limitation and recheck condition. A successful list/read call does not prove Spain registration, inbound reachability or production entitlement.

B2BR-02 — Prepare provider action. The owning invoice feature supplies the original invoice/action identity, route/profile version, direction, representation reference/hash and approved execution owner. The adapter selects either JSON creation or structured-file import for that profile. It must not choose between them dynamically. It records requested transport and document type. If provider defaults can apply, the profile defines permitted equality or compatibility checks. Missing, stale or contradictory evidence returns a hold before transmission.

B2BR-03 — Execute provider operation. The adapter saves a durable attempt before a mutation. It sends the protected API key through the approved secret boundary and sends the explicit X-B2B-API-Version. It records safe correlation data and the returned X-B2B-API-Request-Id where supplied [B2BR-S06]. It never logs a key, webhook secret, invoice body or presigned/private document URL. A local timeout before confirmed transmission can retry under policy. A timeout after possible transmission enters OUTCOME_UNKNOWN.

For structured import, send_after_import=true can queue asynchronous sending for sending transports. A 201 import response proves provider creation/import, not final delivery. The documented provider may replace invalid or incompatible requested transport/document codes with defaults [B2BR-S03]. The adapter therefore compares returned/observed values with the approved profile before reporting progress.

B2BR-04 — Record provider response. The adapter saves the provider invoice ID, account ID, API version, request ID, returned state, actual transport/document type, source time and redacted diagnostic. It then hands the observation to the owning invoice/lifecycle feature. 401/403 becomes an access or scope failure; 404 remains resource absent-or-inaccessible unless a stronger contract distinguishes it; 409 is a state conflict; 422 is input/catalogue validation; and 429 is throttling. These categories do not establish retry safety for a mutation [B2BR-S06].

B2BR-05 — Process provider webhook. The ingress uses the exact raw request body required by the selected contract. It verifies X-B2Brouter-Signature, timestamp and HMAC before deserialised data can affect state. It applies the approved replay window and secret version. It stores event code, provider event identity where supplied, invoice/account identity, triggered time, observed time, payload digest, API/event schema version and verification result. Duplicate delivery returns the prior processing result. An older event can add evidence but cannot blindly regress a derived state. Public version 2026-06-26 documents received_invoice.created and received_invoice.state_change; the selected subscription and fixture tests must prove availability [B2BR-S02/S04].

B2BR-06 — Reconcile missed observations. Reconciliation uses the original account and contract profile. Invoice listing is paginated and supports date/update filters in public documentation, but public evidence does not prove a gap-free cursor [B2BR-S05]. The proposed strategy uses bounded overlap, deterministic ordering where available, stable provider invoice identity and durable deduplication. It records requested range/pages, observed maximum, classification count, unresolved pages and completion time. The checkpoint advances only when the covered range is durably classified. Provider outage, rate limit or changing pages pauses advancement.

B2BR-07 — Resolve unknown outcome. The reconciler searches with stable account, invoice business identity, request correlation and content/reference evidence allowed by the selected contract. Exactly one proven match links the original operation. Proven absence permits repeat only if the approved repeat policy also prevents a late original effect. Several or weak matches remain unresolved. Manual resolution needs separate permission, reason and evidence. It cannot delete or replace the original attempt.

B2BR-08 — Preserve continuity and release. A route transition changes selection for eligible new work only. Existing invoices keep B2B Router account, provider invoice, version, transport/document and lifecycle context. The exit coordinator identifies retrieval, webhook, reconciliation, audit and records dependencies before deregistration, key revocation or secret destruction. Current authority is rechecked for every historical action. Where the original channel cannot remain active, an approved replacement channel is appended with provenance.
The table is a binding candidate, not an approved endpoint allow-list. B2BR-Q01 selects the exact version and operation catalogue.

B2BR-R01
The adapter must implement only the capability subset approved for one contracted product, API version, environment and Spain scope.
B2BR-R02
The adapter must bind every request to tenant, represented legal entity, stable provider account, environment, credential version and explicit API version.
B2BR-R03
Provider connection readiness must not activate or change a Sage route.
B2BR-R04
Outbound, inbound, lifecycle, document retrieval, webhook and reconciliation readiness must be recorded independently.
B2BR-R05
The adapter must use one approved outbound payload strategy per contract profile and retain the exact representation reference/hash.
B2BR-R06
The adapter must persist durable intent and immutable action context before an external mutation.
B2BR-R07
The adapter must retain requested and actual provider transport/document values and hold incompatible substitution.
B2BR-R08
A provider 201, queued state or API acknowledgement must not be reported as recipient delivery, buyer acceptance or reporting success.
B2BR-R09
A possible external effect with unknown outcome must reconcile before repeat unless the selected operation has proven idempotency for the same identity/input/window.
B2BR-R10
Webhook ingress must verify the selected contract's signature, timestamp/replay policy and secret version before state use.
B2BR-R11
Webhooks must be deduplicated and correlated using stable provider identity or an approved composite; delivery time alone is insufficient.
B2BR-R12
Reconciliation must tolerate overlapping pages/windows and must not advance its checkpoint before durable classification.
B2BR-R13
Raw provider state, code, actor/provenance, source time, observation time and mapping version must remain available.
B2BR-R14
Protected credentials and webhook secrets must use approved custody, rotation and redaction controls; application contracts expose references only.
B2BR-R15
Sandbox, staging and production configuration and keys must remain isolated. The same base URL for sandbox/production does not weaken key/environment validation [B2BR-S01].
B2BR-R16
Route/profile/API-version changes must apply prospectively. Historical invoices retain original provider context.
B2BR-R17
VeriFactu/tax-report configuration, IDs and outcomes must remain separate from private invoice exchange.
B2BR-R18
Metrics and logs must exclude secrets and customer invoice content and must not use customer identifiers as metric labels.
B2BR-R19
Numeric limits, service levels, retry budgets, replay windows and retention periods require contracted or measured evidence and an owner.
B2BR-R20
Country-rule isolation tests must prove that Spain identity, routing, public-copy and reporting rules do not become defaults for another country.

ac:layout-cell.h2: Part 3 Logical Service Interactions and Data Inventory

tr.td: B2BR-INT-01
Global API/Onboarding → Connection: configure and qualify a B2B Router binding.
Customer/delegate authority; expected connection version; no route mutation.
B2BR-INT-02
Connection → Trust: resolve a protected API-key or webhook-secret reference.
Least-privilege service identity; secret value never enters business response/log. Rotation invalidates affected qualification.
B2BR-INT-03
Connection/adapter → B2B Router read surface: observe account/capability.
Explicit environment/version/account; bounded read; record provider request ID and freshness.
B2BR-INT-04
Exchange → adapter: execute one outbound action.
Frozen action/profile, one executor, durable attempt and input digest; unknown mutation reconciles.
B2BR-INT-05
Adapter → B2B Router create/import surface: create the selected provider invoice operation.
Protected credential, explicit version, account and provider correlation; no blind repeat.
B2BR-INT-06
B2B Router → webhook ingress → Lifecycle: submit a raw provider observation.
HMAC/timestamp verification, event identity/dedupe and invoice/account correlation; quarantine failure.
B2BR-INT-07
Reconciliation worker → B2B Router list/get surface: recover missed or unknown outcomes.
Original account/profile, bounded overlap, stable invoice identity and safe checkpoint.
B2BR-INT-08
Adapter → Receiving/Records: deliver an authenticated provider source file and metadata.
Source identity, digest, media/profile, capture receipt and access control; notification alone is insufficient.
B2BR-INT-09
Adapter → Lifecycle: append raw provider status/error evidence.
Provider version, provenance and mapping version; no destructive overwrite or inferred actor.
B2BR-INT-10
Exit/Records → adapter: assess and release historical provider dependencies.
Separate authority, dependency list and provider confirmation; route change alone does not revoke access.

ac:layout-cell.p: Logical error categories are INVALID_INPUT, UNAUTHORISED_SCOPE, CREDENTIAL_INVALID, CAPABILITY_NOT_READY, PROVIDER_VALIDATION, PROVIDER_CONFLICT, PROVIDER_THROTTLED, PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE, OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, EVIDENCE_UNTRUSTED, MAPPING_UNDETERMINED and HISTORICAL_ACCESS_BLOCKED. The actual API owner must map these to the existing common error contract rather than create a second vocabulary.

ac:layout-cell.p: Pilot evidence must include tenant/account isolation, secret rotation, callback destination control, raw-body signature verification, replay and duplicate handling, parser/file limits, malware controls, unknown-outcome recovery, pagination under concurrent arrival, throttling/backpressure and historical access after route change. Tests use synthetic parties and identifiers only.

Operations views must show capability qualification age, provider/API version, credential health without secret values, webhook freshness, reconciliation coverage/backlog, unknown outcomes, mapping gaps, throttling, provider incidents and continuity dependencies. Numeric alert thresholds and service objectives remain open until provider commitments and pilot measurements exist.
